answer: Each identity may occupy only one vacant coordinate on a published atlas of scarce influence slots. Occupancy requires locking an opal, a non-transferable uniqueness bond whose serial cannot be split or reused. Rewards and withdrawals remain buried under a dune of delayed settlement that recedes only after peers confirm the coordinate is unshared; a colliding slot or a reused serial slashes every linked opal. Fielding N keys therefore costs N distinct bonds, N exclusive atlas coordinates, and N waiting periods, so capital, scarce slots, and delay all scale with farm size.
